objects.original: Predictably weighted mixed increments of two distinct coordinates of one Brownian motion.
objects.reconstructed: For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). Let Delta_i^n B_j=B_j(t[n,i+1],omega)-B_j(t[n,i],omega).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/BrownianMixedQuadraticVariation.lean: The full module constructs the unit projection (B_j+B_k)/sqrt(2) from the same hB and uses the same weights.

domains.original: Finite Euclidean coordinate set, arbitrary T≥0 and the given sample measure/filtration.
domains.reconstructed: Omega measurable; kappa finite with decidable equality; mu a measure (no finite-measure instance is stated); filtration on R_+; B:R_+ x Omega->R^kappa; distinct j,k in kappa; T>=0; weight a_n,i:Omega->R for n in N and 0<=i<2^n; C real.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/BrownianMixedQuadraticVariation.lean: No T>0 or usual-conditions premise is introduced; probability/finite measure follows from Brownian laws where needed.

quantifiers.original: Uniform second-moment weight bound over all levels and cells; then dyadic level→infinity.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally Omega,kappa,instances,filtration,mu,B,hB,j,k,hjk,T,weight,hAdapted,hWeight,C,hC. The weight hypotheses hold for every n and every i; then n tends to infinity.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/BrownianMixedQuadraticVariation.lean: The public target repeats exactly the producer's weight quantifiers then selects its second conjunct.

assumptions.original: Distinct coordinates; weights in L² and measurable at their left endpoints; one bound C.
assumptions.reconstructed: The vector Brownian properties just described hold. j!=k. Every a_n,i is strongly measurable with respect to the left-endpoint sigma-algebra filtration(t[n,i]), and belongs to L^2(mu). There is one given C with integral a_n,i^2 dmu<=C for all n,i.

conclusion.original: The second moment of the literal mixed sum tends to zero.
conclusion.reconstructed: The real numbers integral_Omega (sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} a_n,i(omega)*Delta_i^n B_j(omega)*Delta_i^n B_k(omega))^2 dmu tend to zero as n->infinity.
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/BrownianMixedQuadraticVariation.lean: The target is a projection of the producer's proved L²-membership and second-moment limit, so source mean-square terminology is justified.

scopes.original: Mean-square convergence, no a.s. statement; T=0 included.
scopes.reconstructed: The asserted convergence is of these second-moment integral values. No separate integrability statement for each full squared sum is printed. T may be zero. No usual-conditions or finite-mu assumption is separately included.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/BrownianMixedQuadraticVariation.lean: No hidden integrability is assumed merely because Lean's integral is total; the preceding theorem proves it.

constant_dependencies.original: C independent of level and cell.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: C is a single uniform bound independent of n and i; it can depend on the already chosen family of weights and preceding data. No explicit convergence rate is stated.
constant_dependencies.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/BrownianMixedQuadraticVariation.lean: C remains uniform; the projection adds none.
